newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest-July 8.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest-July 8.

text.p: News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising,
Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and People

PARIS - WPP, the world's largest advertising and marketing group, is seeking to strengthen its market share in public relations and design in France, chairman Martin Sorrell tells afternoon newspaper Le Monde. (Reuter)

PARIS - French media and communications group Havas says it signed a deal with advertising, direct marketing and public relations firm Publicis under which it will sell its 50 percent stake in Metrobus and 33.3 percent stake in Mediavision.

PARIS - French private television station M6-Metropole Television is rated as the most popular general channel, overtaking its bigger and older rivals, according to a six-monthly survey published by advertising weekly Strategies.(Reuter)

PARIS - France's national daily newspapers are missing from news stands on Tuesday as printers' unions launch a 24-hour strike. Some dailies, in statements read on the radio, urged readers desperate for the day's news to consult their Internet sites.

PARIS - The audience share of TF1, France's largest private television channel, rose slightly in June from May, while that of public channel France 2 fell, according to a monthly survey from French audience measurement body Mediametrie. (Reuter)
PARIS - An asset swap between French pay-television group Canal Plus and Germany's Kirch media concern carves up two big European markets and moves the spotlight to Italy and Spain.

LONDON - Britain's Thorn Plc says it is withdrawing from its domestic rental operations in France, Benelux and Finland, which it estimates will result in a non-operating exceptional provision of around 30 million stg ($50.5 million). (Reuter)

LONDON - Shares of Allied Domecq Plc rose as a press report renewed talk of a possible link with LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton of France. The Sunday Times said Allied could link with LVMH if the French group were unsuccessful in its bid to persuade Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc to abandon their alliance and instead pursue a three-way drinks merger.(Reuter)
